title: Command and Code Injection via eval/system
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x on POSIX hosts (system/exec/shell_exec/passthru and backticks shell out via /bin/sh; disable_functions can remove them but is a deployment, not code, guard)
security_mechanism: system(), exec(), shell_exec(), passthru(), proc_open() and the backtick operator hand the whole string to /bin/sh -c, so ; | && $() ` in a value like $host terminate the intended command and start attacker-controlled ones. eval() executes attacker text as PHP source directly. Dynamic dispatch constructs — $fn() variable functions, call_user_func with an input-derived name, and $$variable indirection — let the request choose which function runs. mail()'s fifth parameter is appended to the sendmail command line, so a crafted value such as -X/tmp/log invokes sendmail options from the request.

source_sink_clues.source: Request parameters interpolated into command strings, function/method names, variable variable names, or mail() additional parameters.
source_sink_clues.sink: system / exec / shell_exec / passthru / proc_open / backticks; eval; $fn() and call_user_func with input-derived names; mail() fifth argument

tracking_guards: Require escapeshellarg() on every interpolated value (or proc_open with an argv array) so metacharacters cannot break out; require a fixed allowlist mapping input to callable names before dynamic dispatch; require mail() extra parameters to be compile-time constants.
not_candidate_when: The command string is entirely constant, every dynamic value passes through escapeshellarg before interpolation, dispatched function names resolve through a fixed allowlist array, or the eval target is a constant string with only numeric validated input.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html
